title: Introduce tenant GPU allocator TF module and strict state boundaries
author: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Adds a new terraform module modules/tenant-gpu-allocator that centralizes tenant-scoped GPU nodepool provisioning, enforces strict tfstate boundaries per-tenant, and introduces a state-migrator plan for existing clusters. Motivation: private installs have accumulated ad-hoc GPU nodepools and cross-tenant state collisions. This PR creates an opinionated allocator, minimal IAM roles, and a migration path so operators can isolate GPU state per tenant and roll forward/rollback safely.

What changed (single-line body):
- New module: modules/tenant-gpu-allocator (API: tenant_id, gpu_profile, azs, node_count_range, affinity_constraints, taint_profile, lifecycle_policy)
- New module: modules/tenant-tfstate-prefix (wraps backend config with per-tenant key_prefix + state-locking improvements)
- Network: modules/gpu-network (small subnets & NAT egress for GPU nodepools, optional private-loadbalancer CIDR mapping)
- IAM: modules/minimal-gpu-roles (least-privilege role for nodepool lifecycle & limited KMS decrypt for image keys)
- Migration tooling: scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh + examples/migrate-tenant-gpu.md documenting import plan and rollback steps
- Examples: examples/tenant-gpu-allocator/ (template that wires allocator + network + iam)
- Tests: terratest/gpu_allocator_test.go (basic plan/apply dry-run) and workflow updates to run unit plan checks

Checklist: 
- [x] Introduce module with interface and docs
- [x] Provide migration plan and dry-run script
- [x] Add IAM least-privilege roles and explain KMS usage
- [x] Add CI plan checks and terratest skeleton
- [x] Add notes for rollback and emergency revert

Commits (high level):
- feat(gpu-allocator): initial module scaffolding + example usage
- feat(state): add tenant-tfstate-prefix backend wrapper and lock improvements
- feat(network): isolated gpu-network module with optional egress mapping
- feat(iam): minimal roles + policy docs and tests
- ops(migrator): add tfstate-migrator.sh and migration docs
- test(ci): add terratest skeleton + GH workflow plan check
- fix: IAM policy edge-case for cross-account image sharing

Files changed (high-level):
- modules/tenant-gpu-allocator/main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, README.md
- modules/tenant-tfstate-prefix/backend.tf, README.md
- modules/gpu-network/*.tf, README.md
- modules/minimal-gpu-roles/*.tf, policies/*.json
- examples/tenant-gpu-allocator/*
- scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh (bash script for sequential state move + validation)
- terratest/gpu_allocator_test.go
- .github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml (adds plan check for allocator directories)

Design notes and rationale: 
- State boundaries: Deployments that share a single tfstate for multi-tenant GPU resources led to accidental cross-tenant modifications during upgrades. The tenant-tfstate-prefix module standardizes the backend key prefix per-tenant and adds an opt-in state lock TTL increase for long-running migrations. This keeps existing backends but prevents accidental overlapping keys by convention and validation.
- Allocation model: the allocator emits a canonical nodepool resource per tenant and supports parameters to restrict AZ spread, GPU model selectors, and taint/affinity profiles. We opted for an explicit allocator rather than implicit terraform module repetition so that future autoscaler/lease mechanisms can hook into one place.
- IAM: Minimal roles scoped to only nodepool lifecycle, autoscaler IAM hooks, and limited KMS decrypt access for images. We avoided broad compute.* permissions and documented how to extend role trust for cross-account image registries.
- Network: Dedicated small subnets for GPU pools reduce subnet exhaustion and make egress policies simpler for private installs. The module can reuse an existing VPC or create a tenant-local subnet.

Migration path (operators): 
1) Run scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh --dry-run --tenant <id> to get a plan of keys to move and resources to import.
2) Create a new tfstate bucket prefix using modules/tenant-tfstate-prefix and verify lock acquisition.
3) Use the migrator to sequentially import nodepool resources into the tenant prefix and validate with terratest/gpu_allocator_test.go plan-only mode.
4) Apply new allocator module pointing to the tenant prefix. Verify nodes come up and autoscaler behaves.
5) If rollback needed, use the migrator --rollback to restore previous state keys. The script uses S3 object copying + DynamoDB lock handoff for safe restore.

Rollout / safety controls: 
- Migration script is intentionally conservative: dry-run is mandatory for the first run, and the script requires operator confirmation.
- We increased TF plan check timeouts in CI for these directories to account for larger plans.
- Added explicit outputs for exported resource ids so downstream consumers can detect changed resource addresses.

Testing & CI: 
- Local terratest harness: quick plan/apply with mocked providers (does not spin GPUs in CI).
- GH workflow: terraform-plan.yml now runs against changed allocator modules and fails fast on driftable changes.
- Manual validation steps documented in examples/migrate-tenant-gpu.md.

Backwards compatibility and migration considerations: 
- No forced changes to existing tfstate layout unless operator runs migrator. The modules are opt-in; operators can keep legacy layouts while they migrate tenants incrementally.
- Change to IAM roles may require a short maintenance window for nodepool replacements if image KMS keys are constrained.

Security considerations: 
- IAM policies are principle-of-least-privilege; cross-account access is documented but not enabled by default.
- The migrator uses temporary credentials and enforces MFA for production runs via operator instructions.
